title: Language Access in South King County
pitch: Measures where families in South King County speak a home language that the public services around them do not actually serve.
description: Demand comes from Washington's 2024-25 school enrollment data (36,775 families, 140 languages); supply is 6,272 scored agency-language pairs across 51 agencies in seven sectors, each backed by an evidence link and capture date. The classification rule was written before any data was collected, and a standard Census apportionment method was tested and rejected after validation showed 7.1 points of mean absolute error. The finding: King County's binding translation list, built on 2016 data, omits Dari, the region's second most common home language (3,040 families). It went to the county as a memo, alongside a 4-page Power BI report and a map of access deserts.

title: Provenance Guard
pitch: Detects AI-written text with two independent detectors, and is designed around the cost of being wrong rather than raw accuracy.
description: A Groq LLM semantic classifier and a pure-Python stylometric heuristic — burstiness, type-token ratio, punctuation density — are fused into one calibrated confidence score. The scoring is built around evaluation tradeoffs: a deliberately wide uncertain band and a disagreement penalty that pulls conflicting signals toward 0.5, minimizing the costliest error of flagging human work as AI. A reproducible false-positive mode is documented, not hidden: formal writing and writing by non-native English speakers get misread, so contested calls route to human review through an appeals workflow, with every decision logged as structured JSON and per-IP rate limiting on API spend.

title: TakeMeter
pitch: A fine-tuned classifier benchmarked against a zero-shot baseline — which it lost to, and the analysis explains exactly why.
description: A balanced 200-example dataset was annotated under a mutually exclusive three-class taxonomy, with explicit decision rules written for borderline cases before labeling began. DistilBERT was fine-tuned and measured against a zero-shot Llama 3.3 70B baseline using precision, recall, F1 and confusion-matrix analysis on a held-out test set. The fine-tuned model lost, and the write-up traces why: a small model on roughly 140 examples learned surface form rather than reasoning, with systematic misclassifications pointing to a labeling boundary limitation rather than annotation noise, plus a specification of what data would fix it.

title: patient-sim
pitch: A voice bot that phones a healthcare AI agent, plays a realistic patient, and files the bugs it finds.
description: A websocket server has Twilio dial the agent under test and relays the call audio to the OpenAI Realtime API, which listens and speaks as the patient. Audio stays G.711 mu-law at 8kHz end to end, so nothing is transcoded anywhere, and personas live in YAML rather than in Python. Eleven recorded calls produced eight documented issues, alongside the probes that found nothing, which are recorded too.

title: The Unofficial Guide
pitch: A retrieval-augmented Q&A system over off-campus student housing documents, where every answer traces back to source text.
description: A two-tier chunking strategy feeds cosine-distance retrieval from a ChromaDB vector store, so answers stay grounded in documents a user can verify rather than in model memory. Generation is constrained to retrieved context to cut hallucination, and the system is evaluated on a fixed question set for both retrieval relevance and answer quality. Deployed behind a Gradio interface.

title: PathReview
pitch: A retrieval-augmented agent that reads a developer's GitHub, resume and repos and returns evidence-based portfolio feedback.
description: A multi-tool agent orchestrates GitHub analysis, skill extraction, README scoring and market comparison, with retrieval grounding every claim in the user's actual work rather than in generic advice. Guardrails cover bias detection, content filtering, PII scrubbing and prompt-injection defense. Ships as a Dockerized service with database migrations and a dashboard that tracks improvement over time.

title: FitFindr
pitch: A multi-tool agent whose planning loop branches on what each tool actually returned, instead of running a fixed sequence.
description: Search, outfit suggestion and caption generation are chained through a conditional planning loop, so the next call is decided by the last result rather than by a script. Session state is carried across turns, every tool is wrapped in its own handling for empty results and malformed input, and tool behaviour is covered with pytest so a broken branch surfaces before a user hits it.

title: Job Application Tracker
pitch: Parses job-related email into structured records and reports on them, replacing spreadsheet tracking with a live dashboard.
description: The Gmail API sits behind Google OAuth and feeds a pipeline that turns inbound mail into a queryable record set. The dashboard reports status distribution, activity over time and a customizable watchlist, so the question changes from "what did I send" to "where is everything now".

title: NeighborLink
pitch: A full-stack social platform where neighbours connect through posts, requests, offers and real-time chat.
description: React, Node.js, Express and MongoDB behind JWT authentication and secured APIs. Socket.IO carries live chat, notifications and comments, and the responsive Tailwind interface covers image uploads and profile customization.

title: Bloom
pitch: A Flutter app for mood tracking, habit formation and weekly reflection, backed by cloud persistence.
description: Mood logging captures intensity, activities, triggers and notes, and feeds a daily hub with a progress ring, todos and an evening review. Habits carry completions, streaks and stats; the timeline groups entries by day with mood filters; the weekly review adds a week selector and charts. Local notifications drive a configurable daily reminder, and everything persists to MongoDB Atlas through mongo_dart.

title: CineLog
pitch: A community film-tracking app used as the subject of a structured code review.
description: Users log films they have watched, rate them, and build collections. The project's real output is the review itself: reading an unfamiliar codebase, identifying defects and design problems, and writing the findings up so that another engineer can act on them.

title: Marvel Dashboard
pitch: A dashboard over the Marvel API with summary statistics and a searchable, multi-filter list view.
description: Fetches live API data with React hooks and async/await, then presents summary statistics above a list that can be searched and narrowed by several filters at once. Filters compose rather than replace one another, so a query can be tightened step by step.

title: Campus Bites
pitch: A card-based guide to ten campus food hubs at Minnesota State University Mankato, with locations and links.
description: Ten venues are presented in a responsive card layout, each linking out to its related resource. Built as a self-contained front end with no framework, which keeps the whole thing to a single fast page load.
